scope: Proposition 3.3 of the manuscript “Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2” (preprints/Elliptic-Squares-and-Zilber-Pink-for-Curves-in-A2-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3ecf115570d0b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The connected algebraic monodromy of H is Sp4, and that of P is SO5. This remains true on every fixed finite cover, on a dense open, and for the conjugate families under consideration. The same connected monodromy is obtained by pullback to a smooth connected algebraic variety mapping dominantly to the base curve. Suppose a smooth connected algebraic variety W maps dominantly to two such curves. The connected joint monodromy on the two five-dimensional systems is either SO5 × SO5, or the coarse joint image of W is contained in a polarized isogeny correspondence. If only the first projection varies, its connected monodromy is still SO5.
